text:
Maya: Sharing a compact proposal for a geo onramp playbook 1 we want a product-facing roadmap that connects routing policies, multi-region failover, and clear GTM gates. Draft here: https://redwood.internal/notes/geo-onramp-playbook

Maya: Instead of 'lanes' I'm calling them bands: pilot-band, affinity-band, residency-band. Bands = expected selling motion + operational commitment + default fallback. Goal: make commitments measurable and routable.

Ravi: I like bands. Quick mapping: pilot-band = self-serve hosted pilot; affinity-band = sales-assisted hosted with regional affinity; residency-band = Dedicated/Private with enforced residency.

Sam: Important: every band needs an evacuation and rollback playbook. Last residency cutover we learned region-order matters. We should predefine steps and an owner per step.

Lina: Sales/CE need a one-slide checklist per band: what we promise, what we monitor, what scope is excluded. Keep it <3 bullets.

Maya: Proposal for affinity-band gates: 1) in-region p95 < 280ms under representative load, 2) distributed tracing + request audit logs active, 3) committed capacity documented and fallback policy declared.

Jesse: Add a compliance gate for residency-band: signed residency attestation for regulated customers. That can be a hard gate before we start enforcement.

Ravi: Infra request: a minimal policy DSL that expresses preferred_region, failover_chain, tenant_capacity, enforcement_mode. Infra can own runtime, product must own semantics and tests.

Sam: Infra can prototype the DSL; product team owns the canary harness (prompt sets, traffic cohorts, latency checks).

Maya: Prioritization idea: treat residency-band requests as high-touch leads that route customers to Dedicated/Private sales path. Affinity-band should cover most affinity asks so platform work stays limited.

Lina: Suggest two milestones: B1 = affinity-band alpha (routing primitives + visibility); B2 = residency-band pilot (hard enforcement + contract/billing flow).

Ravi: Timebox B1 to 6-8 weeks with a focused squad. ops-bot: @ops-bot created task geo-onramp/B1 assigned to Maya,Ravi,Sam.

ops-bot: Task created: https://tasks.internal/geo-onramp/B1  due 8w from 3051234567.

Jesse: I'll assemble a customer-fit matrix (top-10 asks) and tag which band they belong to. Sharing by EOD Friday.

Sam: Implementation note: start with passive signals (headers + metrics) then add enforcement later. This avoids broad migrations and gives visibility first.

Maya: Also adding a small "isolation-readiness" metric (0-100) per tenant for GTM to track progress. It will be a 5-check rollup (billing, SLA, perf validation, observability, legal).

Lina: That will help Sales show progress. Keep the checks binary so % is obvious.

Ravi: Add a failure-mode matrix per band: e.g., primary region outage -> fail to next in failover_chain with warning header; if capacity low -> route to reduced-model or degrade noncritical features.

Maya: Good. I'll include a degradation matrix in the PRD.

Sam: Action items recap:
- Jesse: customer-fit matrix (EOD Fri)
- Ravi + Sam: DSL sketch + evacuation/rollback playbook (next Tue)
- Lina: 1-slide GTM checklist + readiness definition (next Wed)
- Maya: fold into PRD and open PR for review

Lina: :thumbsup: please keep commitment language conservative in GTM assets.

Maya: Will do. Ping me to join the PRD review.

Ravi: No blockers from infra besides capacity to staff the prototype.

Jesse: All good, I'll share the matrix.
